## Findings considered and refused

- **526 and 537 each hold an internal ano teleia** (526 "Τελαμώνιος· εὖ δέ μιν ἔγνων·"; 537 "μετάλμενος· ἐν δὲ κυδοιμὸν"). Refused: 68 of the 3,895 published Iliad units carry an internal ano teleia (e.g. iliad-042 at 101, 109), so the draft is within practice, and splitting would alter `t`, which I may not touch. A later pass or the caller may split if wanted.
- **ἕπονθ’ (474) described as "ἕπω/ἕπομαι".** The θ is the elision of ἕποντο before the rough breathing of ὡς, which points to the middle, while 483 ἕπον is the active; the note hedges with both, and "kept close" is applied to both. I could not settle the lexicon's classification from the sole-source aids, so the hedge stands.
- **ἔργαθεν (437) "it kept off" against the table's ἐέργαθεν (5.147) "cut away".** Different spelling and different object (a shoulder there, "flesh from the ribs" here); the new-renderings reason (subject left bare) stands.
- **Line 434 οὔτησε "thrust at" against table "wounded".** The new-renderings row gives the reason (nothing is wounded) and `i` "stabbed at" keeps the table's `i`. Accepted.
- **Cut at the comma after 499 (unit 497–499) and after 493/495.** The periods run from mid-497 to 501 (about four and a half lines) and 492–497 (six), so the four-line rule permits the cuts.
- **Capital "Oh" in 441 and 452 and "Hades of the famous horses" in 445** are the table's wording; 443–445 and 531, 516, 519, 520, 540–541 reuse the published English verbatim (checked word by word against the packet and iliad-063).
- **"as loud as a man’s head can hold" (462).** Odd but built from χάδε "held" and recorded in new-renderings; rebuilt from the grammar, not remembered.
- **δῖος Νέστωρ "Nestor, heavenly" (510).** Extension of the table's δῖος "heavenly"; accepted as recorded.
- **ἔπαυσας … μάχεσθαι (442)** "made me stop fighting against the Trojans": checked, aorist with accusative and infinitive; the note's "for the moment" is an interpretation, harmless.
- **Note on 462–463 "next two lines show"; note on 440 "formula"**: cross-references checked (440, 522 both end πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν; 9.201, Od. 22.163, 8.112, 10.87, 10.530–531, 7.219, 7.234, 5.652–654, 8.258–259, 5.40–42, 11.264–265, 3.357–358 all verified in the archive or the shipped parts).

# Pass 2 (units.json again, then gloss.json)

Scope: `units.json` re-read unit by unit against `packet.md`, the source text, the published parts (Greek-string search) and the lines pass 1 left alone; every `N.NNN` cross-reference in a note looked up in the source (3.357–358, 5.40–42, 5.652/654, 5.728, 7.219, 7.234, 8.112, 8.258–259, 9.201, 10.87, 10.530–531, 1.240, 3.424, 11.264–265, Od. 22.163 all agree); every repeated line compared with the packet's published `l`/`i` (435, 436, 443, 445, 447, 448, 465, 485, 511, 516, 519, 531, 540, 541: identical where the whole line stands, reworded only where the new line around it forces it); quotation marks and `mark`/`p` recounted (five speeches, “ and ” balanced, `p` on 434, 446, 456, 472, 489, 516, 521, 531 as the packet's ¶). `gloss.json` then read entry by entry: each of the 123 new entries against every line where the form occurs and against the note as it now stands, each of the 13 `__broaden__` entries against `iliad-glossary.json` (old entry whole + " · " + new reading) and its line, and all 433 known forms of the part against their existing entries for a missing reading. Mechanical checks by script: novel-forms = gloss keys (123); no entry reaches 230 characters; no ASCII apostrophe, backtick, digit string, "here" or "line"; every broadened entry contains the old one whole. `t` verified byte-identical to HEAD before and after. Both files written back in the same format (indent 1, no trailing newline). Nothing built, validated or committed.

## Changes made (form/line · severity · what was wrong · what done)

1. 517 (unit "αὐτίκα δ’ ὧν ὀχέων…") · `l`, `i`, `n` · high · The note said "ὧν is Ionic οὖν ‘then’", and `l`/`i` carried "then". Homer does not use ὧν for οὖν; ὧν is the possessive ὅς (genitive plural, agreeing with ὀχέων), as in the published iliad-024 ("from his own chariot", ἀπὸ ὧν ὀχέων) and iliad-030 (ὧν ἵππων ἐπιβάς, "his own horses"), and as the glossary's own entry for ὧν reads; it also answers σῶν ὀχέων at 512. · `l` "And at once he mounted his own chariot", `i` "At once he mounted his own chariot"; the note now says possessive ‘own’, not Ionic οὖν, answering 512.
2. δαμάσσεται (478) · medium · "aor. subj. 3 sg. mid. … (= δαμάσσηται)": the Attic equivalent named was itself an epic spelling, and "mid." read as a middle sense, though the line has ὀϊστός as subject and τόν as object, so the sense is active. · "aor. subj. 3 sg., short-vowel, middle ending but active sense (= Attic δαμάσῃ), in a temporal clause with ἐπεί: ’subdues’".
3. πεύθετ (498) · medium · meaning "’was learning’" against the note ("‘learned’, the imperfect or aorist … without augment"), `l` "did Hector learn of it" and `i` "had not yet learned". · "impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (πεύθετ’ = πεύθετο, Attic ἐπύθετο): ’learned of’".
4. ἕπονθ (474) · medium · lemma ἕπω with "ἕπονθ’ = ἕποντο" is self-contradictory: ἕποντο is the middle (ἕπομαι), and the θ comes from elided τ, so the form cannot be the active ἕπον of 483 (which has its own entry under ἕπω). · Lemma now "ἕπομαι (cf. ἕπω ’be busy about’) — follow; with ἀμφί, throng round; impf. 3 pl. mid., elided and aspirated (ἕπονθ’ = ἕποντο, θ for τ before the rough breathing)".
5. ἐπισσώτρων (537) · medium · "tyre": the table (5.725), the shipped iliad-034 and pass 1's change of `l`/`i`/`n` at 534–537 all have "tires". · "tire".
6. `__broaden__` αἵ (537) · low · the added example read "’and those from the tyres’" (same house point). · "tires"; the reading itself (relative, fem. nom. pl., with τε, continuing a list) is needed: the old entry has the τε relatives only for "of the Trojan women" and "in a simile".
7. κλονέων (496) · low · quoted meaning ’driving in confusion’ against `l`/`i` "throwing the plain into confusion". · ’throwing into confusion’.
8. ἄλλυδις (486) · low · quoted ’one this way, another that’, the wording new-renderings turns down; `l` is "one this way, one that" (as shipped odyssey-066). · ’one this way, one that’.
9. βαλόντες (454) · low · "with περί or πρό in tmesis, ’having cast around, forward’": πρό is not in this part (προβαλόντες at 529 is its own form with its own entry). · "with περί in tmesis, ’having cast around’"; the " · also ’having put’" reading kept (it is the Odyssey's entry for the same spelling).
10. `__broaden__` κελεύθου (504) · low · the added reading ("gen. of separation after χάζοντο: ’from the way’") repeats the old parse and meaning (fem. gen. sg., gen. of separation, "from the road"); only the governing verb differs, which iliad-067 pass 2 held does not call for a broadening. · Entry removed (13 → 12 `__broaden__` entries; 15 with the three additions below).
11. `__broaden__` πάντα added (437) · low · πάντα … χρόα is masc. acc. sg. agreeing with χρόα, but the old entry gives neut. acc. pl. first and masc. acc. sg. only "agreeing with a name" (Αἰγιαλόν τ’ ἀνὰ πάντα). · Old entry whole + " · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with χρόα: ’all (the flesh)’".
12. `__broaden__` ὁπότε added (492) · low · ὡς δ’ ὁπότε … κάτεισι is ὁπότε with a present indicative in a simile (κάτεισι is indicative; the subjunctive would be κατίῃ), a construction the old entry (opt. in a general clause; aor. subj.) does not give. · Added " · also + pres. indic. in a simile: ’as when’ (ὡς δ’ ὁπότε … κάτεισι ’as when … goes down’)".
13. `__broaden__` ἔξω added (457) · low · "ἔξω τε χροὸς … ἕλκε": ἔξω governs the genitive (note: "genitives of separation"), but the old entry is "adv." only. · Added " · also prep. + gen. of separation: ’out from’ (ἔξω … χροὸς ’out from the flesh’)".
14. ὁμίλει (502), βαῖν (518) · low · "unaugmented" with no Attic equivalent named (runbook: Homeric forms name it). · "(= ὡμίλει)" and "(= ἔβαινε)" added.

Count: 1 high (item 1), 4 medium (items 2, 3, 4, 5), 9 low (items 6–14; item 14 covers two forms); 14 entries.

## Findings considered and refused (pass 2)

- **αὖε (461), ἀνέσσυτο (458), ἄϊεν (463), ἰάχοντος, πεύκας etc.: no Attic equivalent named.** Refused for αὖε: the augmented form of αὔω cannot be settled from the allowed sources; ἄϊεν, ἀνέσσυτο (augmented, root σευ-): Attic has no ordinary counterpart in use. Left as is.
- **The other 11 `__broaden__` entries** (γένηται, πλευρῶν, πὰρ, σῶν, τῇ, ἀλέεινε, ἄν, ἅρμ, ἦρχ, ἧκε, ὅπως): each old entry found in `iliad-glossary.json` and kept whole; each new reading checked against its line (471, 437, 499, 512, 499, 542, 504, 528, 472, 539, 459) and found needed. Closest call, τῇ at 499 ("where"): the old entry gives only the route sense ("by which way") and the adverb "by that way, there", so the locative relative is new; kept.
- **κτεριοῦσί "give funeral rites to, bury with honour"** against `l` "render funeral rites to": the entry is a dictionary sense, the `l`/`i` follow the Odyssey's "render … funeral honours"; no conflict. Kept.
- **ἐρύουσι "future in sense"**: the note says the same of ἐρύουσι and καθαιρήσουσι; kept.
- **δαφοινοὶ "deep-red, tawny … exact sense not certain"**: agrees with the note (tawny, blood-red or gore-reddened not known). Kept.
- **χειμάρρους entry "’winter torrent’"** against `l` "a winter-flowing one": the entry quotes `i` and the lemma sense "winter-flowing" stands in front of it; kept as shipped in iliad-027.
- **Known forms read for a missing reading** (all 433): besides items 11–13, none needed one. Closest calls, kept: εἷος at 488 (entry gives "while, until"), ὅσον at 462 (entry "as far as", the same word as "as much as" in the adverbial sense), εὐρὺ at 527 (same parse as the old "agreeing with μετάφρενον"), πολλὸν at 495 (the old "masc. acc. sg., agreeing with ἱδρῶ" is the same parse), ὄφρ’ at 477 (the old "while + subj. in a general clause" covers "as long as … ὀρώρῃ"), κατ’ at 434 and κατὰ at 507 (both readings already listed), νῆας ἔπι at 520 (listed word for word).
- **531 note "(see 8.503 and the Odyssey)"**: 8.503 shares only the phrase καλλίτριχας ἵππους, not the whole formula line; the note says "see", not "same line", so kept.
- **Units left unchanged after rereading:** all `l`/`i` pairs, the 14 repeated lines, quotation marks, `mark`, `p`, and every grammatical label in the notes other than item 1 (spot-checked word by word against the Greek: 439 γνῶ, 450 κιχήμενον, 456 ἕλκε, 465 ἵκετο, 472 ἦρχ’, 489 οὖτα, 497 πεύθετ’, 503 νέων, 507 τριγλώχινι, 520 ἔπλετο, 535 ἄντυγες).
